frequency_question: What proportion of statutory review periods for major nuclear agreements result in successfully enacted joint resolutions of disapproval?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 agreements or major nuclear cooperation pacts submitted to Congress where a joint resolution of disapproval was introduced; excludes informal consultations and non-statutory executive arrangements.

cases.name: US-Iran Nuclear Agreement review mechanism attempts (historical)

provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 3 named (10.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 30+ formal submissions examined across the history of Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act; zero joint resolutions of disapproval have ever successfully become law over a veto or without one.
known_gaps: Some minor technical amendments or non-substantive 123 agreements bypass intense congressional floor action entirely.
skeleton: Total historical submissions of major 123 agreements where a resolution of disapproval was formally debated vs. total successfully enacted over total elapsed decades.
multiplier: 0 enacted out of approximately 30+ total submitted 123 agreements across 7 decades.
validity_reason: Statutory timelines and structural hurdles for overriding presidential vetoes on foreign agreements remain fixed under the Atomic Energy Act.
